title: Friend who always forgot Secret Santa
author: Storytime
hook: Every year, one friend in our group forgot to bring her Secret Santa gift. This year, we planned to kick her out. Then we found out why.
story: Our friend group has done Secret Santa for eight years. Fifty dollar limit. And every single year, our friend Nora shows up empty handed. She always says the same thing. I'm so sorry, it's coming in the mail. It never comes. Last year, the person who drew her got nothing. Again. So this year, the group chat decided. If Nora forgets one more time, she's out. I was the one who sent the message. Two weeks ago, I was volunteering at the children's hospital downtown for my company's charity day. In the toy room, I saw a shelf with a little sign. Donated every December by Nora K. In memory of Sam. Sam was Nora's little brother. He passed away at that hospital when he was seven. I knew that. I didn't know the rest. The nurse told me Nora brings a bag of gifts every year. Exactly fifty dollars per gift. One for every person in our Secret Santa. Eight years. She never forgot. She just gave our gifts to kids who needed them more. And she never told us. The group chat doesn't know yet. How do I tell them?
caption: she never forgot. not once 🎁 #storytime
sound: a gentle, emotional Christmas music box at very low volume
why: Secret Santa drama starts going viral in mid November, the always forgetting is the setup, the hospital reveal is a powerful twist, and how do I tell them invites heartfelt comments.

title: The locked closet in my new flat
author: Storytime
hook: My new flat had a locked closet. The landlord said it was storage, never to open it. Last night, it was unlocked.
story: I moved into my flat in October. It's in an old building, high ceilings, creaky floors. In the hallway, there's a narrow closet with an old brass lock. The landlord said, that's just storage, don't worry about it. I don't have the key. For a month, I walked past it every day. I'll admit, I got curious. Last night, I came home and the closet door was open. Just a few inches. I nearly called the police. Then I saw what was inside. Shelves. Full of envelopes. Hundreds of them. Every single one addressed the same way. To whoever lives here next. Dated every Christmas from nineteen seventy-one to last year. I called the landlord. He sounded embarrassed. He said, Mrs. Ellis lived in that flat for fifty years. She passed away in the spring. She made him promise to give the next tenant the key in December. He came by to check on the radiator, and forgot to lock it again. I opened the first letter. It said, Welcome home. I hope this flat is as kind to you as it was to me. Fifty years of letters. Should I read one every day until Christmas?
caption: to whoever lives here next ✉️ #storytime
sound: a mysterious music box that turns warm at very low volume
why: Creepy storytime is trending, the locked closet is an instant hook, the letters turn it into a cozy holiday story, and the daily letter idea sets up a natural series.

title: Coworker earns double for my job
author: Storytime
hook: I found out my coworker earns double my salary for the exact same job. Then I found out how he negotiated it.
story: Derek and I started at the same company on the same day, two years ago. Same title. Same team. Honestly, I do more of the work. Last week, a payroll email got sent to the wrong person, and the whole team saw it. Derek makes ninety-two thousand. I make forty-six. Exactly half. I asked him how. He shrugged and said, I just told them I had a better offer from another company. They matched it, plus a bonus. Fine. Smart, I guess. Then I got curious. I asked HR which company he'd mentioned. She said it was a startup called Northpeak Solutions. I looked it up. It has a website. A logo. A team page. And the CEO listed on the team page is me. My name. My face. My LinkedIn photo. Derek built a fake company, made me the CEO, and used it to get a raise. I showed HR. She went completely pale and said, I need to talk to legal. Derek doesn't know yet. He just invited me to lunch to celebrate his promotion. Should I go?
caption: apparently I'm the CEO of a fake company 💼 #storytime
sound: a funky, mischievous bass groove at very low volume
why: Pay transparency is a hot workplace topic, the payroll mistake hooks everyone, finding yourself as the fake CEO is an absurd twist, and the lunch question gets petty advice.
